justification: Fixes the confirmed silent-wrong-data defect in issue #762: the brief handed one shared report_id to flood, bushfire and shadow, and each service's ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE upsert let the last writer clobber the first writer's outputs while the row kept the first product label — the bushfire cache then served flood or shadow outputs merged over all-null defaults, and every re-run re-poisoned the newest row.

pre_impl.existing_data: No stored row changes shape and no migration runs; already-poisoned property_reports rows stay in place but the new sentinel-key cache guard skips them at read time, and a separate approval-gated cleanup DELETE is drafted in the PR body without being executed.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Standalone tool flows poll property_reports by the exact report_id the frontend allocated, so id derivation deliberately happens only at the brief's fetch call sites — the services' own _write_report id handling is untouched and standalone semantics are preserved.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Applies to every future brief run through distinct per-product uuid5 row ids, and to all historical poisoned rows already in property_reports through the cache guard, which skips them at read time rather than backfilling anything.

functions.name: _derive_service_report_id
functions.input: the brief's parent report_id as a uuid4 string plus the satellite product name being fetched
functions.output: a deterministic uuid5 string, stable per parent-product pair and distinct across products, used as the property_reports row id
functions.if_none: a non-UUID parent raises ValueError inside the pool-submitted lambda, which _safe_call converts to a NOT_AVAILABLE DataField for that section

functions.name: _first_valid_cached_row
functions.input: the list of candidate cached rows returned newest-first by the bushfire product and address SELECT
functions.output: the newest row whose outputs dict contains the is_bushfire_prone sentinel key, meaning genuinely bushfire-shaped outputs
functions.if_none: returns None when every candidate is poisoned or the list is empty, so run_bushfire falls through to live compute

functions.name: _first_valid_cached_row
functions.input: the list of candidate cached rows returned newest-first by the flood product and address SELECT
functions.output: the newest row whose outputs contain epi_flood_class or flood_signal, meaning genuinely flood-shaped outputs
functions.if_none: returns None when every candidate is poisoned or the list is empty, so run_flood falls through to live source queries

functions.name: get_shadow_risk
functions.input: address, prop_id, coordinates, optional LEP height, and now an optional caller-supplied report_id for the row the shadow service writes
functions.output: the shadow pipeline outputs dict with run-level confidence merged in, or None when the Railway endpoint is unreachable
functions.if_none: report_id None keeps the previous behaviour exactly, allocating a fresh uuid4 per call for CLI and conveyancing callers

values.value: outputs field of each candidate cached property_reports row
values.if_missing: a row with null or non-dict outputs is skipped like a poisoned row and the scan falls through to the next candidate

values.value: cached row selected by the flood sentinel guard before serving
values.if_missing: None means no valid cached row exists, so the cached branch is skipped entirely and the live source queries run

values.value: report_id parameter threaded into the shadow request payload
values.if_missing: the or-fallback allocates a fresh uuid4 so standalone and CLI callers keep their pre-change row-per-run behaviour

queries.purpose: bushfire cache lookup now fetches the five newest candidates so the sentinel guard can fall through past poisoned rows
queries.where_clause: WHERE product='bushfire' AND address=%s ORDER BY run_date DESC LIMIT 5

queries.purpose: flood cache lookup now fetches the five newest candidates so the sentinel guard can fall through past poisoned rows
queries.where_clause: WHERE product='flood' AND address=%s ORDER BY run_date DESC LIMIT 5

break_it.scenario: Two satellite services finish a brief run back-to-back with the same parent report_id, as in the live Kincumber contamination
break_it.what_happens: Pre-change the second upsert overwrote the first row's outputs while the row kept the first product label, silently serving cross-product data
break_it.how: uuid5 of parent and product gives each service its own row id, so the captured INSERT params for bushfire and flood carry distinct ids

break_it.scenario: The newest bushfire row for an address is already poisoned with flood outputs from the pre-fix era
break_it.what_happens: Pre-change the cache merged the flood blob over bushfire defaults and served an all-null section with fire_signal unavailable
break_it.how: the sentinel guard skips rows lacking is_bushfire_prone and serves the older genuine row, with flood keys asserted absent from the response

break_it.scenario: Every cached row for the address is poisoned so no genuine bushfire outputs exist in the table at all
break_it.what_happens: Serving any candidate would render wrong data, and a naive newest-row read has nothing valid left to return
break_it.how: the guard returns None which turns the cache branch into a miss, falling through to live RFS BFPL compute instead of serving poison

break_it.scenario: A genuine unknown bushfire result stores is_bushfire_prone as null and an over-strict guard treats it as poisoned
break_it.what_happens: Over-aggressive filtering would discard legitimate cached unknowns and force needless live recompute on every subsequent request
break_it.how: the guard tests key presence rather than value truthiness, so a null-valued sentinel key still marks the row as bushfire-shaped

break_it.scenario: A future edit reverts the cache SELECT back to LIMIT 1 while leaving the guard function itself in place
break_it.what_happens: A poisoned newest row would hide the healthy older row again because the guard would only ever see one candidate
break_it.how: a test asserts the executed SELECT contains no LIMIT 1 and keeps the run_date descending order, failing on that regression

break_it.scenario: Someone reroutes a brief call site back to passing the raw parent report_id into a satellite fetch
break_it.what_happens: The clobber would silently return for that product pair while every test touching only the derivation helper kept passing
break_it.how: source-level tests assert all three call sites pass the derivation helper and that the old raw-report_id call strings are gone
